rules.sentence: A recent meta-analysis reported radial nerve palsy in approximately 12.2% of patients with humeral shaft fractures.[14]
The incidence is lower in pediatric populations, with radial nerve palsy occurring in approximately 4.3% of children with humeral shaft fractures.[15]
Radial nerve injuries represent approximately 15% of upper extremity peripheral nerve injuries in the US.
The incidence of radial nerve palsy in the United States (US) is approximately 2.9 cases per 100,000 persons per year.[11]

In the United Kingdom, the annual incidence of radial neuropathy is estimated at 2.97 per 100,000 in men and 1.42 per 100,000 in women, with the highest rates observed among men aged 75 to 84 years.[12]

Connective tissue diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus, may manifest as wrist drop within mononeuritis multiplex, characterized by acute, painful, asymmetric sensorimotor deficits.[8]
Nutritional deficiencies, including thiamine deficiency, may rarely induce focal neuropathies in chronic alcoholism or malnutrition.[9]
Heavy metal toxicity, particularly lead poisoning, remains a relevant global cause of radial nerve dysfunction.[10]
